knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Zero-size reduction dimensions in linear algebra operations may produce uninitialized or inconsistent output
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Backend implementations may not correctly initialize or compute outputs when a reduction dimension is zero, leading to nondeterministic results that depend on uninitialized memory state.

risk_dimensions.shape: Zero-size reduction dimensions and degenerate matrix dimensions
risk_dimensions.dtype: Integer dtypes, particularly torch.long and other integer types
risk_dimensions.memory: Output buffers may remain uninitialized when the reduction dimension is zero
risk_dimensions.device: CPU backend dispatch may exercise backend-specific zero-size reduction handling
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Repeated executions may reveal nondeterministic outputs

failure_mechanism.description: Backend linear algebra implementations may not correctly handle zero-size reduction dimensions, leaving output memory uninitialized or producing inconsistent results.

input_exploration: Explore operations with zero-size reduction dimensions
Vary outer dimensions while keeping one reduction dimension zero
Explore integer dtype combinations including long and other integer types
Test both left and right zero inner dimension cases
constraint_awareness: Integer dtype and CPU backend may follow specialized backend paths with weaker zero-size handling
Repeated execution is required to expose nondeterministic output from uninitialized memory
Zero-size dimensions are valid but often overlooked boundary conditions
oracle_strategy: Run the same operation multiple times and compare outputs for consistency
Compare against a reference implementation that explicitly handles zero-size reduction dimensions
Detect outputs that vary across repeated executions or match uninitialized memory patterns

transferability.reason: The principle applies broadly to linear algebra and reduction operations where a reduction dimension can be zero and backend kernels may rely on uninitialized output memory, including matmul, addmm, bmm, and similar APIs.

important_considerations: Treat zero-size reduction dimensions as a high-risk boundary condition
Combine zero dimensions with integer dtypes and CPU backend to exercise backend-specific paths
Check output determinism across repeated executions
Consider both matrix multiplication and related reduction-style operations
generation_strategy: Generate fuzzing harnesses that construct tensors with zero reduction dimensions, vary outer dimensions and integer dtypes, execute the target operation repeatedly, and compare outputs for nondeterminism or against explicit reference behavior. Avoid hard-coding the original issue's exact shapes or dtype constraints.
